source.title: Inventory Tracking Requirements.
source.body:
# Inventory Management Proposal

Proposed Changes

Track phones and laptops per unit (by IMEI or serial number), and accessories by quantity.
2. Record IMEI/serial at both purchase and sale. This gives you a full trail if police, customers, or suppliers ever ask about a device.
3. Verify IMEIs before buying used phones (for example via the GSMA tools or your local regulator’s checks) to avoid blacklisted or stolen devices.
4. Use a system, not just notebooks: a spreadsheet works to start, but inventory or POS software with barcode scanning saves time and reduces errors as you grow.

Barcodes, Numbers, QR Codes
1. Apple Devices: Apple Serial Numbers to get device information
2. Samsung Devices: Samsung Serial Numbers get device information
3. Manual Data Entry

Device Information Includes
- Interna UUID and SKUS
- Device Brand
- Device Model
- Device Model Number

Variant details
- Storage 
- RAM
- Color
- Screen Size
- Processor 
- region/version
- Serial Number - Unique per unit (Tracks laptops, tablets and phones)
- Barcode / EAN / UPC  (Pricey 1-19 EUR per month - https://www.ean-search.org/ean-api-intro.html using https://github.com/eansearch/ean-search for device lookups.)
- Camera Resolution

Phone-specific identifiers
 - IMEI 1 and IMEI 2 (dual SIM phones have two). This is the single most important field for phones.
 - Network lock status: locked or unlocked
 - Operating system and version at time of sale
 - Activation lock status (Apple iCloud / Google FRP): confirm it’s off before selling, especially for used devices

Condition and grading (critical for used/refurbished stock)
 - Condition: new, open box, refurbished, used
 - Cosmetic grade: e.g. A, B, C, with a written description of scratches or dents
 - Battery health: percentage for phones and laptops; cycle count if available
 - Functional test results: screen, cameras, speakers, ports, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, fingerprint/face ID
 - Repairs or parts replaced: screens, batteries, and whether parts were original or aftermarket
 - Photos of each used unit

Purchase and sourcing
 - Supplier name and contact
 - Purchase date, invoice/receipt number
 - Cost price (and any import duty, shipping, or clearing costs, which matter for true margin)
 - For trade-ins/buy-backs: seller’s name, ID number, phone number, and a signed declaration of ownership. This protects you if a device turns out to be stolen.

Inventory and stock control
 - Quantity on hand (for accessories) or unit-level status (for phones and laptops): in stock, reserved, sold, in  repair, returned
 - Storage location: shelf, shop branch, warehouse
 - Reorder level for fast-moving accessories 
 - Date received, so you can spot slow-moving stock

Sales information
  - Selling price, discount given, final price
  - Date of sale, receipt/invoice number
  - Payment method (cash, M-Pesa, card, installments) and transaction reference
  - Salesperson
  - Customer details: name, phone, email, and ID if selling on credit or for high-value items
  - Profit per unit (selling price minus all costs)

Warranty and after-sales
 - Warranty type: manufacturer, supplier, or your own shop warranty
 - Warranty start and end dates
 - Warranty terms: what’s covered and excluded
 - Return/exchange history and reason
 - Repair history after sale
 - Accessories included in the box (charger, cable, earphones, case), recorded at time of sale to avoid disputes


# Accessories Tracking

Accessories (simpler tracking)
For chargers, cables, cases, screen protectors, and earphones, you usually only need:
 - SKU, brand, compatibility (which phone/laptop models), color, quantity, cost, price, supplier, and reorder level
Higher-value accessories like power banks, smartwatches, and earbuds benefit from serial numbers and warranty tracking
 - This can be used to generate a QR code for stickers to help identify and track device information.

Laptop-specific extras
 - Processor, RAM, storage type and size (SSD/HDD), graphics card
 - Keyboard layout
 - Charger included and wattage
 - Operating system and license status
 - BIOS/MDM lock status, especially for ex-corporate laptops

IMEI numbers will be used to track specific devices and link them to their owners.
